reasoning: A hybrid strategy combines autonomous reasoning to identify obvious shared patterns across instances with external XAI tools to quantify feature importance and detect spurious correlations. This ensures both domain-level intuition and model-level attribution are leveraged to pinpoint features that are present in all misclassified cases and have high model reliance despite lacking semantic relevance to the target variable.

autonomous_tasks.query: Identify which columns are common across all three misclassified instances (13590, 2021, 17473)
autonomous_tasks.expected_output: A list of shared feature names (e.g., education-num=9, marital-status=Married-civ-spouse, relationship=Husband) that appear in all instances

autonomous_tasks.query: Evaluate whether the shared features (e.g., marital-status=Married-civ-spouse, occupation=Craft-repair, etc.) are semantically relevant to income prediction or could be spurious due to co-occurrence with other features or dataset biases
autonomous_tasks.expected_output: A justification for why these shared features may be spurious or non-essential despite being highly correlated in the model

tool_selection.reasoning: SHAP provides stable, interpretable feature importance scores across instances, enabling identification of features with high attribution in the model for all misclassified cases. LIME and Integrated Gradients offer local interpretability to validate feature impact. Sensitivity analysis confirms whether removing a feature changes prediction significantly, indicating spurious dependency. Combining these tools ensures we detect both shared features and their model-level attribution, distinguishing spurious signals from meaningful ones.
